sections.h2: Who handles your Granville County tax bill
sections.html:
Granville County Tax Administration, at 919-693-4181, is the one number for valuation, relief programs and billing. Almost every question routes there.

A contracted appraiser stands in for the assessor on informal real estate appeals. The next step up, the Board of Equalization and Review, is made up of the county commissioners. The county has five municipalities: Butner, Creedmoor, Oxford, Stem and Stovall. Each town's levy appears on the county bill beside its own line.

Owners outside every municipal boundary, and owners inside Stovall, also pay a fire district tax. That money is restricted to fire protection.

The county rate is 0.631 per $100 of value. A town or fire district rate is added on top, depending on where the parcel sits. Inside a town, add the town rate. In the countryside, or in Stovall, add the fire district rate.

Granville County rates per $100 of value
JurisdictionRate per $100
County rate0.631
Fire service district0.06
City of Oxford0.57
Town of Butner0.42
City of Creedmoor0.58
Town of Stovall0.355
Town of Stem0.35

The county's formula is value times the combined rate, divided by 100. Call the tax office to confirm which districts touch your address, since the boundaries decide which rows apply.

Pay a current-year bill during the window of July 1 to August 15 and the county trims 1.5% from it. Past that window the bill is due September 1, and interest does not start until January 5 passes.

  • July 1 to August 15: 1.5% off for early payment.
  • September 1: regular due date, G.S. 105-360.
  • January 5: the final day to pay face amount.
  • Afterward: 2% through February 1, then three-fourths of one percent for each month or fraction.

Options include the website, a mailed check, the counter, your bank's bill pay and the phone. The county's card vendor also runs e-billing that sends an alert whenever a balance, an owner or a due date changes. A mailed check is judged by postmark, which means the last day is a risky day to drop it in the mail.

The next countywide revaluation is set for 2030. Until then, assessed real estate values reflect market conditions on January 1, 2024.

Granville finished a reappraisal in 2018 and first ran on the state's eight-year schedule. In 2020 the Department of Revenue warned that tax values and sale prices were drifting apart, so the commissioners moved to a six-year cycle. Average home sale prices in the county are up 27% since 2021.

A frozen valuation date works two ways. A later market swing, up or down, is not grounds for a different value. A factual error on the parcel record is fair game at any point in the appeal window: wrong acreage, a demolished building still listed, or a structure that was never there.

In a revaluation year the sequence runs like this: notices in January or February, informal appeals February through April, board hearings starting in April, board adjournment in June and a new rate on July 1.

Appeals climb three rungs: the assessor's informal review, then the commissioners acting as the equalization board, then the state Property Tax Commission.

  • Fill out the county's Assessor's Appeal Form early. The appraiser replies in writing, and if you accept the reply, you are done.
  • Still unhappy? Call 919-693-4181 and request a board hearing. Hearings start near the end of April and continue into early June.
  • The last rung is written notice to the Property Tax Commission, due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290).

When there is no revaluation that year, appeals open January 1 and close on the day the board adjourns, which is never later than early June. An owner whose value was changed by a notice mailed after adjournment gets extra time.

Personal property has its own clock. Contest within 30 days of the first notice, attend a conference, and send the board a written request within 30 days after the final answer. Vehicles are handled on a separate county page. A review might leave the figure alone, drop it or raise it, so weigh that before you file.

sections.h2: Relief programs that could lower a bill
sections.html:
North Carolina offers three ways to cut a homestead bill, and Granville's tax office (919-693-4181) can tell you which suits you. You can take just one.

  • Age 65 and up, or disabled: a slice of your home's appraised value is exempt, whichever is bigger between $25,000 and half. Income has to stay under the 2026 limit of $38,800. Statute: G.S. 105-277.1.
  • Disabled veteran: $45,000 of value is exempt regardless of age or income. Statute: G.S. 105-277.1C.
  • Circuit breaker: tax is limited to 4.0% or 5.0% of your income, and whatever is shaved off sits as a deferred lien. Statute: G.S. 105-277.1B.

Form AV-9 goes to the county assessor, who has to accept it through June 1. Sell a circuit breaker home and three fiscal years of deferred tax come due, so raise it with your closing agent early.

Taxes you owe become a lien on the parcel dating to the January 1 listing date (G.S. 105-355), and penalties, interest and costs ride along.

Write to Granville County Tax Administration and ask for the amount due on the current bill, plus any deferred amount tied to a relief program. Give both numbers to the person running your closing.

Ignored long enough, a balance can lead to a sale on the courthouse steps (G.S. 105-374). You can still redeem before the sale is confirmed, and paying in full ends the matter. Your buyer's deed is recorded in Oxford, where the seller pays the state excise tax of $1.00 per $500, or fractional part, before the clerk accepts the filing.

A cash sale skips a lender's payoff and appraisal steps. The tax lien still has to be cleared at or before closing, so ask for the figures early and keep the receipt for your file.

sections.h2: Granville County housing at a glance
sections.html:
The county has 61,421 residents and 25,685 housing units. About 77.1% of occupied homes are owner-occupied, and the middle value of an owner's home is $247,700. A household averages 2.52 people.

About one resident in five is 65 or older (20.0%), so the age-based exclusion is worth asking about. These are countywide midpoints, and a specific parcel can sit well away from them. Before you list, pull your own bill and compare the town and fire district lines to the rate table above.

faqs.q: What is Granville County's county tax rate?
faqs.a: The county rate is 0.631 per $100 of value. Your town or the fire district adds its own rate on top.

faqs.q: Does paying early save money in Granville County?
faqs.a: Yes. Current-year bills paid from July 1 through August 15 get 1.5% off. The regular due date is September 1.

faqs.q: By when must a Granville County value be challenged?
faqs.a: In a year without revaluation, the deadline is the day the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, no later than early June. Begin with the assessor's form.

faqs.q: Who can claim the $25,000 or half-value exclusion?
faqs.a: A homeowner age 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, who lives in the home and keeps income under the limit, which is $38,800 for 2026. Apply on Form AV-9.

faqs.q: Where is a Granville County deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds in the courthouse at 101 Main Street, Oxford, phone 919-693-6314. The seller pays the excise tax to that office before recording.
